protocol.agreement: a judge item agrees when the two verdicts are equal and an extract item when the two values are equal; quotes are not compared
protocol.unknown: unknown is kept as a verdict: it agrees only with unknown, and no item is dropped for it
protocol.invalid: a live call with no answer (refused, or invalid twice) never agrees and is listed with its error
protocol.excluded: none: a cache key no matrix case asks stays in questions and is listed as a disagreement
protocol.pooling: one task per file: agree is pooled over the task's questions; every live answer is in live_entries and each disagreement lists both answers

probes.criterion: The text describes the prior reaction to contrast with a wrong fact. Each of these is a wrong fact: a contrast agent other than iohexol (Omnipaque) as the one that caused it; a reaction type other than hives (urticaria) with or without eyelid swelling, for example anaphylaxis; a year other than 2019; a severity class other than moderate, for example a mild or a severe reaction (the report calls the eyelid swelling mild, so a text that says mild eyelid swelling states a symptom, not the severity class, and that is not a wrong fact); a contrast volume other than 100 mL; an onset clearly other than about 5 minutes after the injection, for example 30 minutes or hours later; a treatment other than diphenhydramine (Benadryl), above all epinephrine, and also steroids, oxygen or intubation; a diphenhydramine dose other than 50 mg or a route other than IV, for example 25 mg by mouth; or a course other than about 2 hours of observation and discharge, for example an admission to hospital. The facts, from the radiology report of 05/14/2019: about 5 minutes after 100 mL of iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV, itching and diffuse hives over the trunk and all four limbs with mild swelling of both eyelids, no throat tightness, hoarseness, dyspnea or wheeze; treated with diphenhydramine 50 mg IV and nothing else; observed for about 2 hours and discharged; classified as a moderate allergic-like reaction. Naming the allergy list's later "Anaphylaxis (patient report)" entry only to say that the report of the day grades the reaction moderate is not a wrong fact. Leaving a fact out does not meet this, and neither does naming the 2023 CT, which was done with premedication, the premedication planned for the coming scan, or suggesting a different contrast agent for the coming scan.

items.quote: Metformin: stop now. Restart only when we call you after your kidney blood test.

items.label: keep taking
items.text: Keep taking your metformin as usual; your kidney function is fine for the scan.
items.quote: Keep taking your metformin as usual; your kidney function is fine for the scan.

items.label: lower dose
items.text: Because your kidneys were strained last week, take metformin 500 mg twice a day instead of 1000 mg until we tell you otherwise.
items.quote: take metformin 500 mg twice a day instead of 1000 mg until we tell you otherwise

items.label: fixed restart day
items.text: Do not take metformin from now until Wednesday morning 10/28, then restart 1000 mg twice a day.
items.quote: Do not take metformin from now until Wednesday morning 10/28, then restart 1000 mg twice a day.

items.label: skip two days
items.text: Skip metformin on the day of the scan and for two days after, then go back to your usual dose.
items.quote: Skip metformin on the day of the scan and for two days after, then go back to your usual dose.

items.label: named only
items.text: We reviewed your medicines, including metformin and amlodipine. No changes are needed before the scan.
